nodes.text: For any function $f:\mathbb{N}\to \mathbb{N}$ the property that, for almost all $\alpha$\[\left\lvert \alpha-\frac{p}{q}\right\rvert < \frac{f(q)}{q}\]has infinitely many solutions with $(p,q)=1$, is equivalent to\[\sum_{q\geq 1}\phi(q)\frac{f(q)}{q}=\infty.\]

#999 : [Er64b] number theory | diophantine approximation The Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture . It is easy to prove that the latter follows from the former. Erdős proved this in the special case when $f(q)q$ is bounded. The full conjecture was proved by Koukoulopoulos and Maynard [KoMa20] .
